sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Use read-only replicas to offload read-only query workloads (read scale-out)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: read scale-out lets you 'offload read-only workloads using the compute capacity of one of the read-only replicas, instead of running them on the read-write replica', 'intended for ... logically separated read-only workloads, such as analytics'; enabled by default on new Premium, Business Critical and Hyperscale databases; route with ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly; check with DATABASEPROPERTYEX(DB_NAME(), 'Updateability') = READ_ONLY; replica latency 'tens of milliseconds to single-digit seconds'. That a failover restarts in-flight transactions on the primary is from memory (to verify).

brief.situation: You are a data analyst at Corvin Garden Supply. At 11:00 you started a year-over-year sales report (a scan of five years of order lines) from your SQL client against the shop's Azure SQL database (Business Critical). Since then checkout has slowed from under a second to eight seconds. The midday flash sale starts at 12:00.
handover: The database is Business Critical; nobody has used its read-only replica yet.
The report is due to the sales director by 14:00.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the primary database that takes checkout writes, its read-only replica and your report.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why checkout slowed, what you changed, and how reporting avoids it next time.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: My year-over-year report, one large scan of five years of order lines, ran on the read-write primary and took 97% of the CPU that checkout's small transactions need.

parts.label: Changed
parts.criteria: Moved the report, not the database.
parts.modelAnswer: Cancelled my session and re-ran the report with ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly on the Business Critical replica; checkout returned to 0.6 seconds. A failover would have cut off every checkout.

parts.label: Next time
parts.modelAnswer: The team's reporting profile uses the replica, and big historical reports will run on a nightly copy in the analytics store.

outage.headline: Stop your own query, not the database
outage.body: The load was one analytical query. Cancel that session and run it on the read-only replica; a failover disrupts every transaction.

saleSlow.headline: Analytics and transactions on one copy
saleSlow.body: A large analytical scan competes with small, fast transactions. Run reporting on a read-only replica or an analytical store.

separated.headline: Good: the right copy for the workload
separated.body: You found your own analytical query competing with checkout, moved it to the read-only replica, checked both, and set up the team to report from the right place.

scoring.modelReasoning: Your analytical report, a big scan of years of order lines, is running on the primary that handles checkout's small transactions and is using nearly all its CPU. Stop your own session and run the report on the read-only replica with ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly; a few seconds of replica lag do not matter for a year-over-year view. A failover would interrupt every checkout; storage is unrelated. Make the replica the team's reporting default.
